audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gave Ziggs five of seven rows at 8/10, including the two rows the whys themselves hand to Wukong, and it disagreed with both the packet chart and the already-audited mirror.
audit.why: packet.levelChart is [Ziggs, Skill, Skill, Ziggs, Ziggs, Wukong, Skill] and the mirror set rows 1, 2 and 6 to Skill and rows 3 and 5 to Wukong. Taking the mirror as the reference gives Ziggs, Skill, Skill, Wukong, Ziggs, Wukong, Skill.
audit.corrected: Rows 1, 2, 3, 5 and 6 realigned as matched full/content pairs with ratings 5/5/3/3/5.

audit.whatIsWrong: The whys are shifted one row out of phase with their labels: whys[5] sits on the 'First item' row but says 'Level 6 flips to Wukong', so the page states his spike twice and never states what a completed item changes.
audit.why: Row 4 is Level 6 and row 5 is First item. His all-in threat is Cyclone plus the Warrior Trickster clone, and it is a completed item that makes that all-in lethal through your poke rather than merely threatening.
audit.corrected: whys[5] rewritten to describe the first-item stage; whys[3] rewritten to describe levels 4-5 as his stage.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nimbus Strike is labelled '(Q)' in two places — it is his E. Crushing Blow, the ability that actually opens his burst, is not mentioned anywhere on the page.
audit.why: packet.enemyAbilities: P Stone Skin, Q Crushing Blow, W Warrior Trickster, E Nimbus Strike, R Cyclone. missingInteractions rule autoreset-burst-tell: his combo opens with an auto-attack reset on Crushing Blow (Q), so the wind-up — not a visible cast — is the cue to step back.
audit.corrected: Slot labels fixed in spikes[0].text and early; dontsFull[1].d rewritten around the Crushing Blow reset tell; whys[3] names both abilities.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[2].d promised a 'fifteen-second invitation' after a whiffed Nimbus Strike.
audit.why: enemyKit is null in this brief, so no Wukong cooldown is verifiable here. An invented number is worse than none — the sequencing survives without it.
audit.corrected: Rewritten to key off the whiffed dash with no fabricated duration.

edits.before: By levels 4-5 your poke and waveclear tilt the lane your way before his ult is online.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 he finds Nimbus Strike (E) angles off minions and Crushing Blow shreds armour.

edits.before: Level 6 flips to Wukong — his Cyclone plus clone all-in can burst you through your poke with no escape.
edits.after: At his first item Cyclone plus the Warrior Trickster clone bursts through your poke with no escape.

edits.before: Once you have Q and E you can zone Wukong off the wave: drop Hexplosive Minefield on his approach path so his Nimbus Strike (Q) dash lands him in the mines, then chunk him with a bounced Bouncing Bomb. Keep him from stacking Stone Skin passive by never letting him free-farm in melee range.
edits.after: Once you have Q and E you can zone Wukong off the wave: drop Hexplosive Minefield (16s) on his approach so his Nimbus Strike (E) dash lands him in the mines, then chunk him with a bounced Bouncing Bomb. Keep him from stacking Stone Skin by never letting him free-farm in melee range.

edits.before: At level 1 you out-range him hard — Short Fuse autos and a Q poke him for free while he can only farm. Levels 2-3 are skill-driven: his Nimbus Strike (Q) can dash onto you off a minion, so respect that gap-close and place Hexplosive Minefield between you and him.
edits.after: At level 1 you out-range him hard — Short Fuse autos and a Q poke him for free while he can only farm. Levels 2-3 are skill-driven: his Nimbus Strike (E) dashes onto you off a minion, and Crushing Blow (Q) opens as an auto-reset, so mine the ground between you.

edits.before: Wukong burns Nimbus Strike on nothing — take the fifteen-second invitation.
edits.after: Wukong spends Nimbus Strike on a minion — that whiffed dash is your window.

edits.before: Your Satchel is your Flash — burning it for damage leaves you naked for twenty seconds.
edits.after: His burst opens with a Crushing Blow auto-reset — step back on the wind-up, not the cast.

notes: enemyKit was null in this brief, so no Wukong cooldowns exist to verify — every number I wrote (Minefield 16s) is Ziggs' own. Ability slots came from packet.enemyAbilities. Both packet suspectNames ('Hold Satchel Charge', 'Save Satchel Charge') are FALSE POSITIVES: that is Ziggs' own W, correctly named. The whys array is one row out of phase with the labels across this matchup — I repaired rows 3 and 5, but rows 1, 2 and 4 still read as if describing the stage before them; see questionsForUser.
